queryName.Length > 0 in front of the empty-non-terminal clause. The two readings differ only for the root, whose queryName is empty, and there the clause asks whether a next name ends in '.' followed by nothing - in a dot. Every next name is compared after TrimEnd('.'), which leaves no trailing dot to find, so the clause is false for the root whether the guard lets it run or not. The guard spares the work and decides nothing

CompareHashes(hash, owner) > 0 in FindCover, the lower end of an NSEC3's span - and the same argument as 525 below, which is the point of listing both. A name whose hash equals an owner matches that record, and VerifyNSEC3 looks for a match before it looks for a cover, at the queried name and again at every ancestor on the way up. Nothing can be handed to FindCover whose hash equals an owner in the set, and the code added since the first sweep calls FindMatch but never FindCover

Left[i] < Right[i] ? -1 : 1, which sits inside if (Left[i] != Right[i]). The two readings differ only when the two octets are equal, and the guard one line above is exactly the statement that they are not. The same shape as 573 below, in the hash domain instead of the name domain

CompareCanonical(Name, owner) > 0 in Covers, the lower end of an NSEC's span. The two readings differ only when the name equals the owner, and no caller can put that case in front of it. For the queried name, VerifyNSEC's NODATA loop returns before Covers is reached whenever any record owns it - and the empty-non-terminal clause added since the first sweep comes after that loop too. For the wildcard, the very next clause asks whether a record owns that name and answers the same way in the same iteration, so the || is true either way. The guard at the other end of the span has no such cover, and a test kills it
comparison < 0 ? -1 : 1, inside if (comparison != 0). The same argument as 506: the value that separates < from <= is the one the guard above excludes

proof != Insecure || provenBy is null, after ProveNoDelegationSigner - which says one thing twice. Every one of its returns pairs Insecure with the parent whose keys signed the proof, and every other verdict with null, so the two operands are true together and false together, and where two operands always agree, or and and cannot differ. The other mutation of the line, != read as ==, returns Insecure before the parent's keys are authenticated, and a test kills it

rrSet.Count > 0 in DenialSignedBy. Read as >= 0 it is always true, and it differs only for an RRSIG over an NSEC or NSEC3 the authority section does not hold: the mutation then asks whether that signature verifies over an empty set. Whatever the answer, verified.AddRange adds the empty set, which is nothing, and asking has no side effect - ValidateRRSig catches everything, and VerifiedByOneOf only computes. The list the proof is read from is the same. The && beside it, read as ||, adds every RRset unverified, and a test kills that

dotIndex < 0 in GetParentZone, which answers '.' for a zone of one label. Its one caller left is the chain walk, and it asks whether the answer is null and nothing else - while both readings return a name, '.' or what follows the first dot, for every input that gets past the line above. The first sweep's argument, that Zone.TrimEnd('.') cannot begin with a dot because a DomainName cannot hold an empty leading label, still holds and is no longer needed
